```{r setup, include=FALSE}
repo <- normalizePath(params$repo, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
source("examples.R", local = TRUE)
package_version <- read.dcf(file.path(repo, "DESCRIPTION"), fields = "Version")[1L, 1L]
needed <- c("cache/examples.rds", "cache/ssb_comparison.pdf")
if (!all(file.exists(needed))) cli::cli_abort("Run examples.R prepare before rendering.")
example <- readRDS("cache/examples.rds")
package_files <- c(list.files(file.path(repo, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE), file.path(repo, "NAMESPACE"))
if (!identical(file_hashes(package_files), example$provenance$sources)) {
  cli::cli_abort("The package changed. Rerun examples.R prepare before rendering.")
}
if (!identical(fingerprint(example_code("examples.R")), example$provenance$example_md5)) {
  cli::cli_abort("The model examples changed. Rerun examples.R prepare before rendering.")
}
case_study_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(repo, "analysis/case_study/001_models.R")))
if (!identical(case_study_md5, example$provenance$case_study_md5)) {
  cli::cli_abort("The case study changed. Verify the examples and rerun prepare.")
}
dat <- example$dat
script <- readLines("examples.R", warn = FALSE)
excerpt <- function(name) {
  first <- match(paste0("# ---- ", name, " ----"), script)
  if (is.na(first)) cli::cli_abort("Missing example excerpt: {name}.")
  markers <- grep("^# ---- .* ----$", script)
  last <- min(markers[markers > first]) - 1L
  code <- script[seq.int(first + 1L, last)]
  if (name %in% c("dashboard", "hindcast")) code <- sub("^# ?", "", code)
  code
}
for (name in c("inputs", "scaa", "sam", "ncam", "dashboard", "hindcast", "tidy")) {
  writeLines(c("\\begin{rcode}", excerpt(name), "\\end{rcode}"), paste0("cache/code_", name, ".tex"))
}
writeLines(package_version, "cache/package_version.tex")
escape_tex <- function(x) {
  gsub("([#$%&_{}])", "\\\\\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
}
display <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    out <- ifelse(x == trunc(x), format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
                  formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "fg"))
  } else {
    out <- as.character(x)
  }
  out[is.na(x)] <- "NA"
  escape_tex(trimws(out))
}
input_table <- function(name, columns) {
  x <- dat[[name]][, columns, drop = FALSE]
  indices <- c(1L, 2L, nrow(x) - 1L, nrow(x))
  cells <- lapply(x[indices, , drop = FALSE], display)
  rows <- vapply(seq_len(4L), function(i) {
    paste(vapply(cells, function(column) column[i], character(1)), collapse = " & ")
  }, character(1))
  gap <- paste(rep("\\tablegap", length(columns)), collapse = " & ")
  header <- paste0("\\textcolor{white}{\\textbf{", escape_tex(columns), "}}")
  writeLines(c(
    paste0("\\begin{inputtable}{", paste(rep("r", length(columns)), collapse = "|"), "}"),
    paste0("\\rowcolor{tamnavy}", paste(header, collapse = " & "), " \\\\ \\hline"),
    paste0(c(rows[1:2], gap, rows[3:4]), " \\\\ \\hline"),
    "\\end{inputtable}"
  ), paste0("cache/table_", name, ".tex"))
}
input_table("catch", c("year", "age", "obs", "unit"))
input_table("index", c("year", "age", "survey", "samp_time", "obs", "q_block", "unit"))
input_table("weight", c("year", "age", "obs", "unit"))
input_table("maturity", c("year", "age", "obs"))

rsvg::rsvg_pdf(file.path(repo, "man/figures/logo.svg"), "logo.pdf")
```

```{=latex}
\renewcommand{\micro}[1]{{\fontsize{7.4}{9.7}\selectfont #1\par}}
\renewcommand{\texttt}[1]{\inlinecode{#1}}
\pageheader{tinyAM :: MODEL REFERENCE}{Settings, equations and the population assumptions they represent}
\begin{minipage}[t][160mm][s]{.325\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}
\begin{mathbox}{Abundance and survival}
\micro{N is start-of-year abundance. Each year, survivors move forward one age; survivors in the terminal age remain in the plus group. Let $Z=F+M$; recruitment is $R_t=N_{t,1}$.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat N_{t,a}&=N_{t-1,a-1}e^{-Z_{t-1,a-1}},\\[-1mm]
\widehat N_{t,A}&=N_{t-1,A-1}e^{-Z_{t-1,A-1}}\\[-1mm]
&\quad+N_{t-1,A}e^{-Z_{t-1,A}},\\
\log N_{t,a}&=\log\widehat N_{t,a}+\eta^N_{t,a}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\micro{$\eta^N_{t,a}$ is the abundance deviation; see Variation in N, F and M for process choices. \texttt{init = "exp"} initializes older ages from exponential survivorship; other choices are \texttt{"free"}, \texttt{"latent"}, \texttt{"mono"}, and \texttt{"capped"}. Age indices $1,\ldots,A$ run from the youngest modeled age to the plus group.}
\micro{For $t\ge2$, non-plus ages use the first survival equation.}
\end{mathbox}\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Recruitment}
\micro{\texttt{rec\_settings}: \texttt{process = "off"} estimates a mean without process deviations; \texttt{mu\_form = \string~ factor(year)} gives annual recruitment. \texttt{"rw"} gives a random walk. With IID/AR1 residuals, \texttt{mu\_form = \string~ bh(ssb)} or \texttt{\string~ ricker(ssb)} adds a stock--recruit curve.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{RW: }\log R_t-\log R_{t-1}&=\epsilon_t,\\
\log R_t&=\log g(SSB_{t-L})+u_t,\\
g_{BH}(S)&=\alpha S/(1+\beta S),\\
g_{Ricker}(S)&=\alpha S e^{-\beta S}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\micro{$\alpha,\beta>0$; $\epsilon_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_R^2)$. IID has $u_t=\epsilon_t$; AR1 has $u_t=\phi_Ru_{t-1}+\epsilon_t$ and a stationary start. Curves describe medians. Lag $L$ defaults to the youngest biological age; early boundary R is free. No RW + curve.}
\end{mathbox}\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Biomass and spawning biomass}
\micro{Spawning biomass sums mature biomass across biological ages after mortality up to spawning.}
\[
SSB_t=\sum_b n_{t,b}w_{t,b}p_{t,b}e^{-\tau_{t,b}Z_{t,b}}.
\]
\micro{Biomass is $\sum_b n_{t,b}w_{t,b}$. $b$: retained biological age; $n$: its abundance; $w$: weight; $p$: mature fraction; $\tau$: year fraction from year start to spawning (default 0; set \texttt{maturity\$spawn\_time} for age/year-specific values). Hidden ages retain biology/timing and share plus-age mortality.}
\end{mathbox}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t][160mm][s]{.325\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}
\begin{mathbox}{Mean fishing mortality}
\micro{\texttt{F\_settings}: \texttt{process = "off"} with \texttt{mu\_form = \string~ factor(year) + factor(age)} gives fixed separable year and age effects. \texttt{mu\_form = \string~ logistic(age)} gives a rising long-term mean.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
S(a)&=\{1+e^{-k(a-a_{50})}\}^{-1},\quad k>0,\\
\log F_{t,a}&=\beta_F+\log S(a)+\eta^F_{t,a}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\micro{With IID or AR1 process deviations, \texttt{mu\_form = \string~ mono(age)} instead adds cumulative nonnegative log-mean steps. Annual F can depart from the mean through $\eta^F$ (see Variation in N, F and M).}
\end{mathbox}\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Natural mortality}
\micro{\texttt{M\_settings}: \texttt{mu\_supplied = \string~ M0} supplies the baseline mortality surface.}
\[
\log M_{t,a}=\log M^0_{t,a}+\eta^M_{t,a}.
\]
\micro{\texttt{M0} comes from \texttt{pop\_covariates}. M states share age blocks and start in year 2 by default; other cells retain the mean. $\eta^M$ denotes process deviations (see Variation in N, F and M); \texttt{mu\_form} adds log-mean effects.}
\end{mathbox}\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Variation in N, F and M}
\micro{N and M support \texttt{"off"}, \texttt{"iid"}, \texttt{"rw"}, and \texttt{"ar1"}; F supports \texttt{"off"}, \texttt{"iid"}, \texttt{"rw"}, \texttt{"ar1"}, and \texttt{"cor\_rw"}. The equations above use $\eta^N$, $\eta^F$, and $\eta^M$ for these deviations.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{IID: }&\eta_{t,a}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_a^2),\\
\text{RW: }&\eta_{t,a}-\eta_{t-1,a}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_a^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
\micro{AR1 stationary covariance (state/block distances):}
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_{t,a},\eta_{s,b})=
\frac{\sigma_a\sigma_b\phi_t^{|t-s|}\phi_a^{|a-b|}}
{(1-\phi_t^2)(1-\phi_a^2)}.
\]
\micro{F \texttt{"cor\_rw"}: independent annual increment vectors with}
\[
\Sigma_{ab}=\sigma_a\sigma_b\rho^{|a-b|},\quad-1<\rho<1.
\]
\micro{RW starts are unpenalized. \texttt{"off"} sets process deviations to zero.}
\micro{N, F and M have separate process parameters. \texttt{sd\_form = \string~ 1} shares SDs; \texttt{\string~ factor(age)} gives age-specific SDs. \texttt{iid()}, \texttt{rw()} and \texttt{ar1()} terms structure log SD. Ordinary age formulas give $\sigma_a=\exp(X_a\beta_\sigma)$. Shared SDs do not share states.}
\end{mathbox}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t][160mm][s]{.325\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}
\sectitle{}{Survey catchability}{.56\linewidth}\par\vspace{.5mm}
\begin{minipage}[t]{.78\linewidth}\vspace{0pt}
\micro{\texttt{q\_block}: unrestricted age blocks; \texttt{mono(q\_block)}\\
imposes non-decreasing catchability under the default log link.}
\end{minipage}\par\vspace{1mm}
\[
\eta_{q,k}=\beta_q+\sum_{j<k}d_j,\quad d_j\ge0,
\qquad q_k=e^{\eta_{q,k}}.
\]
\micro{Zero steps give exact plateaus. With \texttt{q\_link = "logit"}:}
\[
q_k=\{1+e^{-\eta_{q,k}}\}^{-1}.
\]
\micro{\texttt{\string~ logistic(age)} gives a logistic age pattern. Terms \texttt{iid()}, \texttt{rw()} and \texttt{ar1()} add Gaussian variation; q covariates come from \texttt{index}.}
\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Catch and survey observations}
\micro{Catch and survey observations are linked to population quantities by the predictions below; observed log values have Gaussian errors.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde C_{t,a}&=N_{t,a}\frac{F_{t,a}}{Z_{t,a}}(1-e^{-Z_{t,a}}),\\
\widetilde I_i&=q_iN_{t_i,a_i}e^{-s_iZ_{t_i,a_i}},\\
\log Y_i&\sim\mathcal N(\log\widetilde Y_i,\sigma_i^2),\\
\sigma_i&=\sigma_i^0\exp(X_{sd,i}\beta_{sd}).
\end{aligned}
\]
\micro{$s_i$: survey sampling fraction. Catch/index \texttt{sd\_form = \string~ 1} shares an observation SD; \texttt{\string~ survey} allows survey differences. Baseline SDs and Gaussian formula effects can modify log SD. Predictions are medians; zero/NA observations are excluded, with complete predictions.}
\end{mathbox}\vfill
\begin{mathbox}{Fit and prediction checks}
\micro{\texttt{check\_tam()} checks numerical and statistical diagnostics; \texttt{fit\_hindcast()} evaluates survey forecasts given observed removals and retrospective stability.}
\micro{The joint likelihood includes active process, formula-effect and observation densities. RTMB integrates random effects by Laplace approximation; intervals use local curvature. Standardized residuals $(\log Y_i-\log\widetilde Y_i)/\sigma_i$ depend on fitted, shrunken states. Convergence does not establish identifiability. Hindcasts return log RMSE and retrospective Mohn's $\rho$.}
\end{mathbox}
\end{minipage}
\pagefooter{\sitefooter}

```
